affordance_in_statement: The network architecture strictly separates the relays into two distinct power grids. Conflicts only ever occur between a relay on the first grid and a relay on the second grid. Two relays on the same grid will never conflict. ... the conflict list is guaranteed to adhere to this strict separation.
removal_suggestion: Do not state the two-grid/bipartite promise directly. Re-present the scenario using an indirect, non-obvious physical invariant whose consequences are not immediately recognizable as bipartiteness; otherwise, removing this affordance changes the underlying task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the conflict graph is bipartite and begins with a bipartition-based solution.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Conflicts are guaranteed to occur only between the two separate grids, with no conflicts within one grid.

common_affordance: The guaranteed bipartite structure of the conflict graph

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The BFS implementation contains the direct typo `q.popl` instead of `q.pop()`, causing execution failure before the graph is processed.

Its approach appears to rely on bipartition-side construction rather than the full maximum-independent-set/König-theorem computation, which can miss valid larger independent sets in general bipartite components.

The component-side bookkeeping suggests the same incomplete side-selection shortcut; choosing partition sides component-by-component is not sufficient for a maximum independent set in an arbitrary bipartite graph.

recommended_edit: Replace the explicit two-grid explanation with an indirect scenario description that preserves the same invariant but does not reveal that the conflict graph is bipartite at a glance.
regression_risk: This presentation-only edit may not defeat a model that independently detects bipartiteness from the invariant; removing the guarantee entirely would change the computational problem.
